newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LILEIKIS TO BE TRIED, HEALTH PERMITTING.
newsitem.headline: LILEIKIS TO BE TRIED, HEALTH PERMITTING.

text.p: VILNIUS, June 24 (Vilnius) - The Lithuanian Prosecutor's office said Tuesday that it had decided to put 90-year-old accused war criminal Aleksandras Lileikis on trial for genocide but that his poor health would halt progress for three months.
"There is a decision to put Aleksandras Lileikis on trial for the responsibility of genocide of inhabitants of Lithuania," the prosecutor's office said in a statement.
The statement said that the indictment in the Lileikis case should have been announced last week and given to the court by July 1 but that this was not done due to Lileikis' poor health.
Medical experts came to the decision that the investigation cannot be carried out now because it is a threat to Lileikis' health, the statement said.
According to the conclusion of the medical experts, the investigation can be continued only in three months and only with the permission of a commission of doctors, the statement said.
Lileikis is alleged to have turned over scores of Jews to Nazi-backed death squads during World War Two while he was head of the Vilnius branch of the security under the Nazi occupation.
His U.S. citizenship was revoked last year on the grounds that he had concealed his wartime activities when he entered America. Lileikis returned to Lithuanian last June.
Observers say that Lileikis may have thought his chances were better in front of a Lithuanian court than anywhere else.
Historians say that 94 percent of Lithuania's pre-war Jewish population of 220,000 was wiped out during the war by Nazis and their local minions.
